EUROPEAN COURT 
BY JOSEPH DYNAN 

PARIS, MARCH 18=(AP)-A PROJECT FOR A EUROPEAN SUPREME COURT TO 
PROTECT BASIC FREEDOMS IN THE 15 MEMBER NATIONS OF THE COUNCIL OF 
EUROPE IS EXPECTED TO GET ROLLING TOMORROW. 

THE COUNCIL"Y FOREIGN MINISTERS ARE OPENING A THREE=DAY SESSION 
IN WHICH THEY ARE DUE TO SIGN AN ANNEX TO THE COUNCIL'S CONVENTION ON 

OVIDE A MECHANISM FO 

MINISTERS MAKE UP THE UPPER HOUSE OF THE COUNCIL. A 
SORT OF INTERNATIONAL LEGISLATURE WITH ADVISORY RATHER THAN ACTUAL 
LAW-=M AK ING POWERS. THEY SIGNED THE ORIGINAL AGREEMENT IN ROME 

THE FREEDOMS TO BE PROTECTED, BORROWED FROM THE UNITED NATIONS 
DECLARATION ON HUMAN RIGHTS, INCLUDE RIGHT TO LIFE. FREEDOM OF 
ASSEMBLY, FREEDOM OF RELIGION, FREEDOM OF SPEECH AND THE RIGHT TO 
A FAIR AND PUBLIC TRIAL. THE’ CONVENTION SPECIFICALLY PROHIBITS 
TORTURE, FORCED LABOR AND DEGRADING PUNISHMENTS « 1952 

SIGNING OF THE ANNEX WILL SET OFF ACTION FOR RATIFICATION IN 
VARIOUS MEMBER PARLIAMENTS. TEN RATIFICATIONS ARE NECESSARY TO 
MAKE THE PLAN EFFECTIVE. BRITAIN, NORWAY AND SWEDEN HAVE RATIFIED 
THE CONVENTION WITHOUT WAITING FOR THE ANNEX. THE PROSPECT IS THAT 
THE NECESSARY RATIFICATIONS WILL BE IN AND THE COURT CONVENED BEFORE 
THE END OF THIS YEAR. 

THE CHIEF AGENCY TO PROTECT THESE LIBERTIES IS TO BE THE COURT 
OF 15 JUDGES, ONE FROM EACH MEMBER STATE. IT WILL BE EMPOWERED TO 
HEAR CASES IN A MANNER SIMILAR TO THE PROCEDURE OF THE INTERNATIONAL 
COURT AT THE HAGUE. 

BUT IN THE PROJECTED EUROPEAN SYSTEM THERE ARE TWO DIFFERENCES. 
ONE IS A DEVICE FOR APPLYING SANCTIONS AGAINST AN ERRING GOVERNMENT. 
THE OTHER IS _A SCREENING AGENCY OR COUNCIL WHICH, LIKE THE COURT 
WILL HAVE ONE OFFICIAL FROM EACH COUNTRY. UNDER’ THE PLAN, ITS MAIN

NATALIA, ALREADY ARE IN THIS COUNTRY AND LIVE ON A CALIFORNIA LETTUCE

CTED OF A CRIM °

RUSS IAN AMBASSADOR, AND KILLED HIM IN THE WARSAW RAILROAD STATION,

UNITED NATIONS, N.Y., MARCH 18-CAP)-THE FIRST UNITED NATIONS

VOTED TODAY BY THE SUBCOMMISSION ON FREEDOM OF INFORMATION. A MOVE

TIE VOTE. 

THE 12-MEMBER SUBCOMMISSION VOTED 10-1 IN APPROVAL OF THE LA 
PRENSA MEASURE PROPOSED BY ALFREDO SILVA CARVALLO, EDITOR OF

LA UNION, VALPARAISO, CHILE. ONLY RUSSIA'S VASILY ZONOV VOTED 
AGAINST 1T. THE URUGUAYAN EXPERT, A. POLLERI CARRIO, WAS 
ABSENT.

AND SOCIAL COUNCIL, TO CONDEMN THE SEIZURE IN MARCH 1951, OF LA 
PRENSA, THE BUENOS AIRES NEWSPAPER, AS AN INFRINGEMENT ON FREEDOM 

OF THE PRESS AND TO REFER IT TO THE UeNe HUMAN RIGHTS COMMISSION FOR 
FURTHER DENUNCIATION.

1. JET ENGINES OF 10 ,0OO™PowNDS CURRENTLY ARE BEING DEVELOPED, WITH 
OTHERS BEING DESIGNED WITH A "MUCH HIGHER THRUST," COMPARED WITH’A 
THRUST IN THE FIRST JET ENGINE, 10 YEARS AGO, OF ONLY 1,250 POUNDS, 
(THRUST IS THE POWER MEASUREMENT USED FOR JET ENGINES IN PLACE OF WJ 


(THRUST IS THE POWER MEASUREMENT USED FOR JET ENGINES IN PLACE OF 
HORSEPOWER USED FOR PISTON ENGINES--ONE POUND OF THRUST BEING 
THE EQUIVALENT OF TWO HORSEPOWER AT 750 MILES AN HOUR.) 

2. THE TREMENDOUS TEMPERATURES AND PRESSURES OF JET FLIGHT HAVE 
RENDERED OLD STEEL ALLOYS VIRTALLY USELESS, AND HAVE CALLED FOR THEIR 
REPLACEMENT WITH COBALT, COLUMBIUM, CERIUM AND OTHER METALS WITH HIGH 
MELTING POINTS--AND WITH RESULTING PROBLEMS OF WELDING AND OF ALLOYING 
THEM WITH A BASE METAL. | 

3, JET SCIENTISTS ARE EXPERIMENTING WITH CERAMICS, ALONE OR IN 
COMBINATION WITH METALS, AS HAVING THE GREATEST RESISTANCE TO HEAT. 

4. SEVENTEEN FORGING AND EXTRUSION PROCESSES FOR THE PRODUCTION OF 
JET-PLANE AIRFRAMES ARE BEING BUILT AT A COST OF HALF A BILLION DOL- 
LARS. THE LARGEST, OF 50,000 TONS, WILL BE AS TALL AS A NINE-STORY 
BUILDING AND WILL’ EXERT PRESSURES UP TO 100 MILLION POUNDS. 

"IN THE KIND OF WORLD SITUATION THAT EXISTS TODAY, WE MUST BE PRE- 
PARED TO MAINTAIN OUR MILITARY STRENGTH AT HIGH LEVELS FOR AN INDEF- 
INITE PERIOD OF TIME, ON THE BASIS OF PARTIAL MOBILIZATION, AND STILL 
BE READY FOR TOTAL MOBILIZATION ON PRACTICALLY AN OVERNIGHT BASIS,” 
WILSON SAID. 

"WE CAN BE SURE THAT IN THIS AGE OF ATOMIC BOMBS AND TURBO-JET 
BOMBERS, AN ATTACK WILL BE SWIFT. 

"THE RETALIATION ON OUR PART MUST BE EQUALLY SWIFT AND MUCH MORE 
PUNISHING.® | cand.

WASHINGTON,MARCH 18-C(AP)-A DEFENSE DEPARTMENT OFFICIAL TODAY TERMED 
THE AIRCRAFT PRODUCTION OUTLOOK *"VERY ENCOURAGING." 

CLAY P.BEDFORD, SPECIAL ASSISTANT TO THE DEFENSE SECRETARY, TOLD A 
SENATE SMALL BUSINESS SUBCOMMITTEE ABOUT HIS VISIT LAST WEEK to THE AIR 
MATERIEL COMMAND HEADQUARTERS IN DAYTON,O. 

SUBCOMMITTEE CHAIRMAN MOODY (D-MICH) ASKED HIM ABOUT A PUBLISHED , 
REPORT THAT HE HAD GONE THERE TO "RAISE HELL” ABOUT DELAYS IN AIR- 
CRAFT OUTPUT. THE SUBCOMMITTEE HAS BEEN LOOKING INTO THE EFFECT 
OF THE MACHINE TOOL SHORTAGE ON PRODUCTION. 

"AS MARK TWAIN SAID ABOUT THE REPORT OF HIS DEATH, THE REPORT IS 
SOMEWHAT EXAGGERATED,” BEDFORD SAID. 

"WHAT I WAS DOING AT DAYTON," HE CONTINUED, “WAS INVESTIGATING AND ; 
TRYING TO SCREEN OUT THE MOST CRITICAL SPOTS" IN THE PRODUCTION PROGRAM. © 

WITHOUT NAMING ANYONE HE PRAISED THE WRIGHT-PATTERSON BASE OFFICIALS 
IN DAYTON FOR THEIR HANDLING OF PRODUCTION PROBLEMS, CALLING THEM "HARD 
WORKING YOUNG FELLOWS WITH A LOT OF DRIVE AND PUNCH." 

"IT MAKES YOU FEEL GOOD ABOUT THE DEFENSE OF THE COUNTRY TO SEE 
THAT SORT OF THING," HE SAID.

(300) SIMULATED FLIGHT 

BY FRANK E.CAREY 

WASHINGTON, MARCH 18-(AP)-THE NAVY DISCLOSED TODAY IT HAS DEVELOPED 
\ WHIRLING DEVICE WHICH CAN SIMULATE THE HAZARDS TO WHICH HUMANS AND 
LANES ARE SUBJECTED IN HIGH SPEED, HIGH ALTITUDE FLIGHT. 

CALLED A "HUMAN CENTRIFUGE", THE MACHINE OPERATES LIKE A CREAM SEP- 
MRATOR, OR THE FAMILAR CARNIVAL "WHIP". 

NAVY SCIENTISTS SAID IT OFFERED THE BEST POSSIBLE SOLUTION TO STILL 
JNANSWERED QUESTIONS ABOUT THE PHYSIOLOGICAL EFFECTS OF OPERATING-- 
\ND ESCAPING FROM=-HIGH ALTITUDE, HIGH-SPEED AIRPLANES. IT ALSO IS 
DESIGNED TO TEST AIRCRAFT MATERIALS UNDER STRESS. 

THE MACHINE CONSISTS ESSENTIALLY OF A 50-FOOT STEEL ARM STRETCHING 
IORIZONTALLY FROM A HUGE DRUM. AT THE OUTER END OF THE ARM IS AN 
ALUMINUM =PLASTIC GONDOLA IN WHICH A MAN CAN SIT AND BE WHIRLED) 
TUMBLED AND SUBJECTED TO VARIOUS OTHER FORCES, JUST AS IF HE WERE IN. 
AN AIRPLANE. 

THE GONDOLA CAN BE SPUN, LIKE A STONE ON THE END OF A STRING, AT 
SPEEDS UP T0180 MILES AN HOUR WHILE AT THE SAME TIME BEING SUBJECTED 
TO FORCES OF GRAVITY FAR. IN EXCESS OF THOSE WHICH CAN BE SUSTAINED BY 
MAN OR BY PRESENT-DAY PLANES. THE MACHINE IS WHIRLED BY A 4,000 
HORSEPOWER MOTOR. | 

HUMANS CAN NOT WITHSTAND THE MAXIMUM CAPABILITIES OF THE DEVICE== 
AND STUDIES ALREADY ARE UNDERWAY TO DETERMINE THE LIMITS OF HUMAN 
TESTS. BUT THE MACHINE CAN BE EMPLOYED AT MAXIMUM FOR ANIMAL TESTS. 

THE DEVICE HAS ARRANGEMENTS FOR WATCHING A SUBJECT BY TELEVISION 
AS HE IS BEING TOSSED ABOUT3 A BUILT-IN HIGH-SPEED X-RAY MACHINE 
FOR TAKING IN-FLIGHT" X-RAYS; AND REMOTELY CONTROLLED INSTRUMENTS 
FOR MEASURING HEART ACTION, BLOOD PRESSURE AND EVEN "BRAIN WAVES « 

THE GONDOLA IS ITSELF A’ LOW-PRESSURE CHAMBER DESIGNED TO SIM 
CONDITIONS WHICH MIGHT BE MET AT ALTITUDES UP TO 60,000 FEET. 

AND THERE ARE MEANS FOR STUDYING SUCH POSSIBLE FLIGHT HAZARDS he 
"PILOT BLACKOUT", EXTREME COLD AND HEAT, LACK OF OXYGEN AND "cai tose 
IVE DECOMPRESSION" SUCH AS MIGHT BE CAUSED BY A LEAK IN A PRESSUR 
ES CENTER OF THE

TODAY ‘SCIENCE HAS HAD LITTLE SUCCESS IN T CONTROL GIANT SNAILS, 


THE PEST THREATENS THE COCOANUT CROP ON ALL PACIFIC ISLANDS. 

HE TOLD THE U.N, TRUSTEESHIP COUNCIL THE FIRST EXPERIMENT WAS TRY- 
ING TO TEACH CHICKENS AND TURKEYS TO EAT THE SNAILS. AFTER FOUR 
EXPERIMENTS, SCIENTISTS FINALLY REPORTED 100 PER CENT SUCCESS IN 
TEACHING ONE FLOCK OF CHICKENS TO MAKE SNAILS THEIR FOOD. THEN THEY 
REPORTED THERE JUST WEREN'T ENOUGH FOWL IN THE ISLANDS TO TEACH AND 
MAKE LT WORTHWHILE TURNING THEM LOOSE ON THE SNAILS. 

ANOTHER SCEME. ALSO PROPOSED FOR PACIFIC ISLANDS OF OTHER TRUST 
COUNTRIES, WAS TO IMPORT A SPECIES OF WASP, KNOWN TO B RTAL ENEMIES 
OF THE SNAILS. TO STING THE SNAILS TO DEATH AND EAT TH GS.

AS GUAM--WHERE THEY DIED OF STARVATION WAITING FOR A PLANE TO FLY THEM 
AROUND TO OTHER ISLANDS. |

ROMULO CALLED ON LIE AND HANDED HIM A LETTER ASKING THAT THE 
ECONOMIC AND SOCIAL COUNCIL CONSIDER THIS PROBLEM AT THE MEETING 
SCHEDULED HERE IN MAY. | 

IN A COMMENT TO NEWSMEN, ROMULO SAID THE COSTS OF LODGING 
AND SUBSISTENCE MUST BE BORNE NOW IN GREAT PART BY THE COUNTRIES 
RECEIVING TECHNICAL ASSISTANCE AND THAT COST HAD PROVED TO BE A HEAVY 
BURDEN, HE SAID HIS GOVERNMENT WANTS THE REGULATIONS RELAXED 
4 ts GOVERNMENTS RECEIVING TECHNICAL ASSISTANCE SHOULD NOT PAY 

IN THE LETTER TO LIE, ROMULO SAID THE PHILIPPINE GOVERNMENT 
"VIEWS WITH CONCERN" THE APPLICATION OF THESE COSTS FOR LOCAL 
TECHNICAL SERVICES AND ADDED$ 

"THIS REQUIREMENT HAS IMPOSED DIFFICULTIES ON RECIPIENT 
GOVERNMENTS SO SERIOUS AS TO NULLIFY THE VERY PURPOSES OF THE 
TECHNICAL ASSISTANCE PROGRAM ITSELF. 

"THE PHILIPPINE DELEGATION HAS, ON VARIOUS OCCASIONS, EXPRESSED 
BEFORE THE ECONOMIC AND SOCIAL COUNCIL AND THE GENERAL As 
THAT TECHNICAL ASSISTANCE IS NECESSARY AND IMPORTANT IN THE GLOBAL 


EFFORT TO HELP RAISE LIVING STANDARDS IN THE UNDER-DEVELOPED COUNTRIES. 


ITS ACTIVE PARTICIPATION IN THE VARIOUS PROGRAMS IS PROOF OF ITS 
ADHERENCE TO THE HIGH IDEALS AND PURPOSES THAT UNDERLIE THEM. 

"EXPERIENCE. HOWEVER, HAS SHOWN THAT THE APPLICATION OF TECHNICAL 
ASSISTANCE POLicy IN THis REGARD HAS RESULTED IN SERIOUS DOFPPCULTIES 
AND DELAYS IN THE LAUNCHING OF PROJECTS AND SPECIFIC PROG IT 
IS FEARED THAT THE DIFFICULTY OF MEETING THE PRESENT FINANCIAL 
REQUIREMENTS FOR TECHNICAL SERVICES WILL IMPEDE THE PROGRESS OF 
TECHNICAL ASSISTANCE PROGRAMS NOT ONLY IN THE PHILIPPINES BUT 
ALSO IN OTHER UNDER-DEVELOPED COUNTRIES."

THIS WEEK HE WAS OBLIGED TO RE-EXAMINE HIS PLANS. HE HAD PLANNED TO 
KEEP HIS COMMAND OVER EUROPE'S DEFENSE UNTIL THE REPUBLICAN CONVENTION 
ACTED. HE BELIEVED HE COULD KEEP POLITICS OUT OF HIS LIFE UNTIL THEN. 

HOW MUCH OF HIS TIME IS OCCUPIED WITH POLITICS AND HE HAS 
REPEATEDLY SAID THAT POLITICS IN THE MILITARY IS ONE OF THE THINGS HE 
FEARS MOST. THUS HIS RETIREMENT FROM COMMAND IS MOTIVATED NOT ONLY 
BY HIS OWN PRINCIPLES BUT BY THE FRIENDS WHO WANT HIM TO RETURN TO THE 
UNITED STATES SOON TO CAMPAIGN ACTIVELY. 

GRUENTHER IS MOST TALKED OF HERE AS HIS SUCCESSOR. HE IS KNOWN TO 
HAVE MORE OF A GRASP OF SHAPE'S AFFAIRS THAN EVEN EISENHOWER. EISEN- 
HOWER HAS BEEN THE BIG NAME AND THE BIG INFLUENCE, GRUENTHER HAS BEEN 
THE ACTIVE EXECUTIVE. 

BECAUSE THE UNITED STATES CONTRIBUTES THE LION'S SHARE OF THE 
DEFENSE STRENGTH AND MONEY, EISENHOWER'S SUCCESSOR IS EXPECTED HERE TO 
BE ANOTHER AMERICAN, BESIDES GRUENTHER, OTHER CANDIDATES, INCLUDE 
UeSe GENeMATTHEW B.RIDGWAY; NBRITISH MARSHAL LORD MONTGOMERY AND 
FRENCH GEN. ALPHONSE JUIN, ALL OF WHOM SERVED UNDER EISENHOWER IN THE 
LAST WAR. THE DECISIVE ANSWER, BE THE CHOICE AMERICAN OR OTHER, : 
PROBABLY WILL REST WITH PRESIBENT TRUMAN.

MODERATES IN THE BRITISH LABOR PARTY DEMANDED ACCELERATION OF 
BRITAIN'S REARMAMENT PROGRAM.TODAY=-A BROADSIDE AIMED AT BOTH THE 
CONSERVATIVE GOVERNMENT AND LEFT WINGERS IN THE LABOR FOLD. 


SPEECHES BY TWO OF THE FORMER LABOR PRIME MINISTER'S TOP LIFUTENANTS 


HERE TONIGHT WARNED AGAINST ANY REDUCTION OF THE ARMSPROCGRAM--AS 
PROGR AN TO THE DANGER POINT. 
UG ELL, FORMER LABOR CHANCELLOR OF THE EXCHEQUER, WARNED 
THAT IF_BRITAIN SLASHES HER DEFENSE SPENDING FURTHER AMERICA MICHT 
TURN ISOLATIONIST AGAIN," WHICH WOULD BRING THIS COUNTRY INTO 
"MORTAL PERIL," 

WOODROW WYATT, FORMER LABOR UNDERSECRETARY OF STATE AND ONE OF 
ATTLEE'S STAUCH 2uPPORTERS IN PARLIAMENT. SAID A REDUCTION OF 
THE NATION'S REARMAMENT PROGRAM WOULD MAKE BRITAIN ®THE LAUGHING 
STOCK OF THE WORLD® AND WOULD ®"GIVE THE SIGNAL FOR STALIN TO GO 
AHEAD AGAIN IN EUROPE," 

CHURCHILL HAD ANNOUNCED PREVIOUSLY THE NATION COULDN'T COMPLETE 
ITS 34600 4000 000 POUND ($10 080,000,000) REARMAMENT PROGRAM WITHIN 
THE SCHEDULED THREE YEARS, BUT WOULD’REQUIRE AN EXTRA YEARe 
THE BEVAN GROUP SAID CHURCHILL'S STATEMENT WAS AN ADMISSION THAT 
THEY HAD BEEN RIGHT ALL ALONG IN CONTENDING THAT THE PROGRAM IMPOSED 


TOO HEAVY A STRAIN ON THE NATION'S FALTERING ECONOMY AND MIGHT ENDANGER 


THE SOCIAL WELFARE PROGRAMS INSTALLED BY LABOR WHEN IT WAS IN POWER. 
IT IS ON THIS ISSUE THAT BEVAN AND HIS FOLLOWERS HAVE BOLTED FROM THE 


ATTLEF LEADERSHIP OF BRITAIN'S SOCTALIST MOVFMFNT ANT HAVF MANF A STRONG 


BID TO TAKE OVER THAT LEADERSHIP THEMSELVES. 3 

IN DENOUNCING THE GOVERNMENT CUT=BACK OF THE REARMAMENT PROGRAM 
WYATT, SPEAKING AT NEWCASTLE-ON-TYNE, SAID BRITAIN'S PRODUCTION LINES 
ALREABY HAD BEEN GEARED FOR FAST REARMAMENT AND ANY SLOWDOWN WOULD 
LEAVE THOUSANDS OF PEOPLE UNEMPLOYED. HE SAID IF THE PROGRAM IS SLOWED 
DOWN BRITISH TROOPS “WOULD BE UNABLE EVEN TO REPLACE ARMS AND EQUIPMENT 
WHICH HAD WORN OUT SINCE 1945." 


Alt | 
"AS FOR THE IDEA THAT WE SHOULD GET 250 MILLION POUNDS (700 :

ABSORB ALL THAT AMOUNT OF ARMS FROM ABROAD. .ANYWAY, THE RESULT 
WOULD BE NOT LESS DEPENDENCE UPON AMERICA BUT FAR MORE 
DEPENDENCE."

ADVICE "IF THEY FELT WE WERE NO LONGER A REAL PARTNER." UNDER THE

THE EGYPTIAN FOREIGN MINISTRY SAID THE CHAMBER'S DISSOLUTION AND

EGYPT'S "NATIONAL ASPIRATIONS"==-DEPARTURE OF THE BRITISH~-WOULD GIVE

THE WAFD TWO WEEKS AGO DECIDED TO WITHHOLD SUPPORT FROM HILALY'S 
GOVERNMENT, AFTER HE SUSPENDED PARLIAMENT FOR 30 DAYS ON MARCH 2 AND Pi ad 
ANNOUNCED HE WOULD WAGE A VIGOROUS CAMPAIGN AGAINST CORRUPTION-- ie 
ALLEGEDLY WIDESPREAD AMONG WAFDIST OFFICIALS--IN THE GOVERNMENT. 

THE DISSOLUTION OF PARLIAMENT HAD BEEN EXPECTED FOR SOME TIME. Poke 

IT WAS THE WAFD GOVERNMENT OF MUSTAPHA EL NAHAS PASHA WHICH LAST : 
OCTOBER ORDERED THE BRITISH OUT OF EGYPT. THIS TOUCHED OFF A SERIES 
OF RIOTS AND BRITISH-EGYPTIAN BATTLES WHICH CULMINATED IN THE DEATH OF 
67 PERSONS AND THE DESTRUCTION OF MILLIONS OF DOLLARS WORTH OF 
PROPERTY IN THE CAIRO FIRE OUTBREAKS. 

AFTER THAT RIOT FAROUK DISMISSED NASHAS PASHA AND HIS GOVERNMENT. 
HIS SUCCESSOR, ALY MAHER PASHA, ATTEMPTED A POLICY OF NEGOTIATIONS WITH 
BRITAIN COUPLED WITH COMPROMISE WITH THE WAFD, BUT GROWING WAFIDST 
INTRANSIEGEANCE MADE THE SUCCESS OF THIS APPEAR UNLIKELY-AND HILALY 
TOOK OVER THE GOVERNMENT ON MARCH 2. 

TWO OF THE WAFD"S STRONGEST LEADERS, FORMER INTERIOR MINISTER 
FUAD SERAG EL DIN PASHA AND FORMER SOCTAL AFFAIRS MINISTER ABDEL FATTAM 
PASHA, WERE ARRESTED LAST THURSDAY. NO CHARGES HAVE BEEN FILED AGAINST 
THEM, BUT SERAG EL DIN, WHOSE INTERIOR MINISTRY CONTROLLED: THE POLICE, 
EARLIER HAD BEEN CHARGED BY THE GOVERNMENT WITH "ADMINISTRATIVE 
RESPONSIBILITY" FOR THE FIRE RIOTS. |

SOUTHEAST ASIA. IT RESEMBLES THE AMERICAN POINT FOUR PROGRAM.

AUSTRIA, MARCH 25-(AP)-THE VIENNA NEWSPAPER DIE 
D TODAY THAT RUDOLF SLANSKY, FORMER VICE PREMIER OF 
CZECHOSLOVAKIA, MAY BE ACCUSED OF BEING PRO-JEWISH IF AND WHEN 

HE COMES TO TRIAL. 

THE PAPER SAID ITS CZECH CORRESPONDENT AT BRNO REPORTED THAT 
"SLANSKY PROBABLY WILL BE ACCUSED OF HAVING MADE IT POSSIBLE For 
THOUSANDS OF JEWS FROM EASTERN EUROPE TO ESCAPE FROM BRATISLAVA 
CIN SLOVAKIA) ACROSS THE AUSTRIAN BORDER.® 

SLANSKY WAS ARRESTED LAST NOVEMBER AND ACCUSED OF PLOTTING AGAINST 
THE COMMUNIST REGIME. HE ALWAYS DENIED RUMORS THAT HIS REAL NAME 
WAS SALTZMAN AND THAT THE FAMILY WAS OF JEWISH ORIGIN. 

THE PAPER SAID THE RECENT ARREST OF LACO CERMAK-PORGES, POLICE 
CHIEF IN BRATISLAVA, AND REPEATED ACCUSATIONS OF ZIONISM VOICED IN 
THE CZECH PRESS AGAINST SLANSKY "REFER WITHOUT DOUBT" TO THIS 
ASSISTANCE TO JEWISH REFUGEES. 

JOSEF TESLA, NEW SECRETARY GENERAL OF THE CZECH COMMUNIST PARTY, 
IN A SPEECH LAST MONTH SAID SLANSKY HAD ADMITTED INTELLECTUALS 
BOURGEOIS ELEMENTS AND JEWS INTO THE COMMUNIST PARTY WITHOUT PROPERLY 
CHECKING THEIR LOYALTY, AND THAT SOME OF HIS CLOSEST COLLABORATORS 
WERE OF JEWISH ORIGIN.

WASHINGTON, MARCH 25-(AP)-TWO REPUBLICAN SENATORS DISAGREED TONIGHT 
ON URETRER-U.N. FORCES SHOULD CONTINUE THE LONG-DRAWN-OUT TRUCE TALKS 
IN KOREA. 

SEN ALEXANDER SMITH OF NEW JERSEY, SECOND RANKING REPUBLICAN ON THE 
SENATE FOREIGN RELATIONS COMMITTEE, SAID THE "ONLY WAY TO GET AT AN

BRITAIN. FRANCE AND THE UNITED STATES URGED IN 1948 THAT ALL OF

GET THE TERRITORY BACK. THEY SPREAD TO MAJOR ITALIAN CITIES MONDAY. 

IN THE RIOTING IN TRIESTE, 160 PERSONS HAVE BEEN INJURED AND 74 
JAILED. IN FIGHTING IN ROME YESTERDAY, SCORES OF STUDENTS AND 30 
POLICE WERE INJURED. MORE THAN 130 PERSONS WERE ARRESTED IN ROME.

ITALY HAD FOMENTED THE DEMONSTRATIONS.

OF THE TRIESTE PROBLEM...

BY GODFREY—ANDERSON 
, MARCH 27-(AP)=FINANCE AND FOREIGN MINISTERS FROM 18 NATIONS 
GATHERED HERE TODAY TO DISCUSS WESTERN EUROPE'S MONEY AND TRADE 
PROBLEMS IN THE.EACE OF MOUNTING-REARMAMENT. 
THE MINISTERS STARTED THEIR THREE-DAY TALKS AT THE HEADQUARTERS 


OF THE ORGANLZATION FOR EUROPEAN ECONOMIC COOPERATION (OEEC), NEAR THE 
PALAIS DE CHAILLOT, WHERE ANOTHER GROUP OF MINISTERS FROM 16 

COUNTRIES IS DEBATING A “GREEN POOL” AIMED AT GROWING EUROPE MORE AND 
CHEAPER FOOD. 

THE MAIN ITEMS ON THE CROWDED AGENDA OF THE OEEC MINISTERS WERE? 

1. HOW TO RAISE BY 25 PER CENT IN THE NEXT FIVE YEARS EUROPE'S 
PRODUCTIVITY IN SIX BASIC FIELDS=-COAL, STEEL, AGRICULTURE, ELECTRICITY 
MANPOWER AND HOUSING, 

2. SUGGESTED REFORMS AND FUTURE ORGANIZATION OF THE EUROPEAN PAY= 
MENTS UNION CEPU), WHOSE ORIGINAL MANDATE IS DUE TO END JUNE 30. 

3. A PROPOSED MANAGING BOARD OF SENIOR TRADE OFFICIALS TO STUDY 
THE PROBLEY OF INCREASED LIBERALIZATION OF EUROPEAN TRADE AND TO DRAW 
UP A NEW *COMMON LIST" OF PRODUCTS WHICH ALL MEMBER COUNTRIES AGREE 
TO FREE FROM QUOTAS. 

THE 25 PER CENT FIVE-YEAR EXPANSION PROGRAM WAS AGREED ON IN 
PRINCIPLE BY A DECLARATION OF THE MINISTERS LAST AUG. @ mits TIME 
THEY ARE STUDYING HOW TO PUT _IT INTO OPERATION. 
THE WORKING GROUPS HAVE BEEN EXAMINING THE PROBLEM IN EACH OF 


THE SIX FIELDS OF ACTIVITY, AND EACH HAS TURNED IN A REPORT. ONLY 

THE REPORT ON COAL HAS BEEN PUBLISHED THUS FAR. IT URGED INCREASED 
SATURDAY WORK IN MINES, ATTENDANCE BONUSES, ANB TAX RELIEF ON OVERTIME 
PAY, 

THE FUTURE OF THE EUROPEAN PAYMENTS UNION. IS SHADOWED_BY_THE 
INSUFFICIENCY OF ITS EXISTING MONETARY RESERVES. 

IT ORIGINALLY WAS FORMED WITH THE UNITED STATES SUBSCRIBING 350 
MILLION DOLLARS. BUT THAT WAS BEFORE THE OUTBREAK OF THE KOREAN WAR 
AND RESULTANT INCREASED PROGRAMS FOR WESTERN REARNAMENT, WHICH THREW 
NEW STRESSES AND STRAINS ON TH Me 

SINCE FINANCIAL ENGAGEMENTS OF MEMBER NATIONS IN EPU WERE 
UNDERTAKEN FOR A PERIOD OF TWO YEARS, THE MINISTERS NOW HAVE TO 
REVIEW ITS WHOLE OPERATION. IN LIGHT OF EXPERIENCE GAINED. 

TODAY, THE UNIONS MAIN TROUBLE IS CHRONIC NEED FOR SUCH 
CONVERTIBLE ASSETS AS DOLLARS AND GOLD. MANY OF ITS MEMBER | 
CTATES ARE HARD UP FOR DOLLARS, TOO, AND SEEM LIKELY TO REMAIN SO 
FOR SOME TIME TO COME. 

$ RECKON THAT A TRANSFUSION OF SOMETHING LIKE 200 MILLION 
EXTRA DOLLARS 18 NEEDED FOR EPU TO KEEP ITS HEAD ABOVE WATER AND VORK 
EN TOWARDS THE AIMS FOR WHICH IT WAS CREATED=-A GENERAL CONVERTISILI

MONIREAL, MARCH 27-C(AP)-THE RT. REVs—¥e¥. TSU, ASSISTANT 


ANGLICAN BISHOP OF HONG KONG, SAID LAST NiG CHINESE COMMUNIST 
GOVERNMENT NOW HAS FULL CONTROL OF THE CHURC HINA AND USES 
MANY OF ITS FACILITIES FOR POLITICAL PURPOSES. 

IN A MEETING AT MCGILL UNIVERSITY, BISHOP TSU, FORMER 
GENERAL SECRETARY OF THE NATIONAL CHINESE CHURCH, SAID THAT BETWEEN 
1949 AND 1951 THE COMMUNIST POLICY FOLLOWED THREE WELL-DEFINED STAGES. 

WHEN THE REDS CAME DOWN FROMTHE NORTH IN 1949 IN THE DRIVE THAT 
EVENTUALLY WON THEM CONTROL OF ALL CHINA, HE SAID, THEY FOLLOWED 
A "COMMON FRONT® POLICY. 

WELL-DISCIPLINED TROOPS PREVENTED DISORDER AND PROTECTED CHURCH 
AND OTHER PROPERTY. COMMUNIST OFFICIALS PROCLAIMED THEMSELVES 
FRIENDS OF ALL WHO WERE SINCERELY INTERESTED IN CHINA'S WELFARE. THEY 
PRESENTED A PROGRAM OF THE "NEW DEMOCRACY" THAT, ON PAPER, GUARANTEED 
FREEDOM OF RELIGION AND OTHER CIVIL RIGHTS. 

THE SECOND PERIOD, "THE PERIOD OF PENETRATION, "BEGAN ABOUT 1950, 
BISHOP TSU SAID. *CARISTIANS SOON FOUND THAT WHEN THE COMMUNISTS 
SAID THEY WERE BRINGING FREEDOM TO "THE PEOPLE" THEY MEANT ONLY TO 
THOSE ACTIVELY IN FAVOR OF THE RED REGIME AND PROGRAM. THE OTHERS - 
BECAME REACTIONARIES AND "ENEMIES OF THE STATE." MANY ENDED UP DOING 
"CORRECTIVE" PENAL LABOR. 

IN 1951, HE CONTINUED, BEGAN THE PERIOD OF "COMPLETE CONTROL." 
ALL BUT THE MOST SUBSERVIENT CHURCH OFFICIALS WERE ELIMINATED FROM 
EFFECTIVE CONTROL OF CHURCH AFFAIRS AND EVEN CHURCH SERVICES WERE 
USED FOR COMMUNIST PROPAGANDA.

THIS WAS PART OF A MESSA CEIVED FROM THREE MEN ON A FLOATING

A REGULAR FLIGHT TO THE POLE. 

THE MESSAGE WAS RELEASED LAST NIGHT BY THE ALASKAN AIR COMMAND 
FOLLOWING RETURN OF THE PTARMIGAN WEATHER PLANE. 

THE ICE ISLANDERS. WHO HAVE BEEN LIVING ON A FIVE-8Y-EIGHT 
MILE CHUNK OF ICE SINCE MARCH 19, CONTACTED THE B-29 AS IT HEADED FOR 
THE POLE ON A WALKIE-TALKIE, THELR ONLY MEANS OF COMMUNICATION WITH 
THE OUTSIDE WORLD. 

IN ADDITION TO THE STOVE AND THERMOMETER, THEY ASKED THE B-29 TO 
PARADROP FIVE GALLONS OF ETHYL ALCOHOL TO Mix WITH THEIR FUEL, A 
THEODOLITE (SURVEYING INSTRUMENT), AND SURFACE OBSERVATION EQUIPMENT 
TO GET A WEATHER STATION IN OPERATION.9 

THEY ALSO ASKED THAT A C-47 SCHEDULED TO LAND ON THE ISLAND WITHIN 
THE NEXT FEW DAYS WITH ANOTHER SCIENTIST AND A COMMUNICATIONS MAN, BRING 
AS MUCH EQUIPMENT AS POSSIBLE.

NAMED FLETCHER'S ISLAND AFTER LT.COL.JOSEPH O.FLETCHER, VETERAN

JUDGE WeCALVIN CHESNUT MADE THE REMARK DURING A DISCUSSION OF

FORT HOOD,TEX.,MARCH 27-(AP)=SECRETARY OF THE ARMY FRAMK.PACE 
TODAY WADED THROUGH ANKLE DEEP MUD ON A WHIRL WIND LOOK AT EXERCISE 
LONG HORN AND SAID THE BIGGEST AIR-GROUND MANEUVER IN U.S. MILITARY 
HISTORY WAS-"REAL REALISM." - 

"IT'S GIVING THE MAN WHO MIGHT HAVE TO GO TO WAR AS REALISTIC 
CONDITIONS AS THEY CAN BE MADE," HE SAID. “ALMOST EVERY OUTFIT HERE 
HAS 30 PER CENT KOREAN VETERANS. THEY TELL ME THIS MANEUVER IS AS 
PHYSICALLY TOUGH AS YOU CAN MAKE IT AND THAT IT IS WHAT A MAN WHO 
MUST GO TO WAR WILL NEARLY FACE." 

A TORRENTIAL RAIN LAST NIGHT TURNED MOST OF THE 1,800 SQUARE MILES 
OF MANEUVER AREA INTO BOG. A FREEZING WIND WHIPPED OVER THOUSANDS 
OF SOLDIERS STANDING, SOUATTING OR WALKING OVER SLIPPERY TRAILS AND 

THE AGGRESSOR FORCES IN THIS MOCK WAR--THE 82ND AIRBORNE DIVISION-- 
STILL WADED THROUGH THE DEFENDING FORCE, THE 47TH INFANTRY DIVISION, 
BUT THE COCKY PARATROOPERS MET WHAT PROBABLY WAS THEIR FIRST BIG 
SETBACK WHEN THEY RAN INTO A BATTALION OF THE CONFIDENT FIRST 
ARMORED DIVISION. 

" ONE BATTALION OF THE FIRST ARMORED WAS COMMITTED TO ACTION THIS 
MORNING. IT KNOCKED OUT 50 PER CENT OF AN AGGRESSOR TANK FORCE OF 26 
TANKS AND CAPTURED SEVEN. THE CREWS OF THE CAPTURED TANKS--GREEN CLAD 
AND WEARING GERMAN STYLE CAPS, HUDDLED DEJECTEDLY IN A MUDDY FIELD, 
SURROUNDED BY INFANTRY ATTACHED TO THE ARMORED UNIT. THEY WERE SENT 
BACK TO THEIR UNITS AFTER FOUR HOURS. 

' "IT WAS AN IDEAL TRAP,* SAID CAPT. FRANK BOWDEN OF FORT WORTH, 
TEX.. COMMANDING COMPANY’B OF THE 701 ARMORED INFANTRY BATTALION. 

HIS COMPANY WAS REINFORCED WITH TWO PLATOONS OF CO. A__OF THE 13 
ARMORED TANK BATTALION. ®WE CAUGHT THESE TANKS LIKE SITTING DUCKS--

AMCISCO-MARCH COURT OF APPEALS TODAY 
REJECTED A PETITION BY A FORMER NEW YORK CITY PSYCHIATRIST THAT THE 
ARMY BE FORBIDDEN TO SEND HIM OVERSEAS AS A PRIVATE. 

DR.STANLEY J.ORLOFF, 27, WAS SENIOR PSYCHIATRIST FOR THE NEW 
YORK CITY DEPARTMENT OF MENTAL HYGIENE AT THE TIME OF HIS INDUCTION 
LAST JULY 21. HE NOW IS IN SEATTLE, UNDER ORDERS FOR SHIPMENT TO THE 
FAR EAST COMMAND. 

ORLOFF ASKED THE COURT FOR AN ORDER RELEASING HIM FROM THE ARMY 
ON THE CONTENTION HE WAS CLASSIFIED ILLEGALLY AS A PRIVATE AND MEDICAL 
TECHNICIAN, INASMUCH AS HE WAS DRAFTED UNDER THE SO-CALLED "DOCTORS" 

HIS ATTORNEY, LLOYD E, MC MURRAY, ARGUED TODAY IF ORLOFF WAS 
REMOVED FROM THIS COURT'S JURISDICTION BY ARMY ORDERS, ANY APPEAL HE 
MIGHT MAKE TO THE COURT, OR TO THE U.S. SUPREME COURT, WOULD BE 
VALUELESS. SHIPPING ORLOFF OVERSEAS, THE ATTORNEY CONTENDED, WOULD 
DEPRIVE HIM OF HIS CONSTITUTIONAL RIGHTS. 

BUT THE APPEALS COURT HELD THAT EVEN IF THE PSYCHIATRIST WERE 
SENT OVERSEAS, HE STILL WOULD BE SUBJECT TO THE COURT'S ORDERS. 

THE "DOCTORS' DRAFT ACT"=-PUBLIC LAW 779--PROVIDED THAT DOCTORS, 
DENTISTS AND ALLIED MEDICAL SPECIALISTS UP TO 51 COULD BE DRAFTED. 

DR. ORLOFF CONTENDED THAT CONGRESS INTENDED TO DRAFT THOSE MEN FOR 
SUCH SPECIAL MEDICAL SERVICES. THE MILITARY ARGUED IN COURT THAT 
ANYONE DRAFTED UNDER THE ACT COULD BE USED FOR WHATEVER DUTY THE 
SERVICE CHOSE. 

THE COURT RULED THAT CONGRESS' INTENT MAY HAVE BEEN. TQ.USE SUCH 
SPECIALISTS AS SPECIALISTS BUT THE WORDS OF THE ACT DIDN* READ 

HAT WAY. 

MILITARY WITNESSES SAID THE AIR FORCE TRIED TO PERSUADE DR. ORLOFF 
TO SERVE AS AN OFFICER AND PRESUMABLY AS A PSYCHIATRIST BUT THAT HE 
S HADN'T COMPLIED WITH REGULATIONS. THEY SAID HE REFUSED TO FILL OUT A 

LOYALTY QUESTIONNAIRE AFTER TAKING A LOYALTY OATH. SO HE WAS RATED

SUPPLY TODAY: TO KEEP ITS DEEENSE AND CIVILIAN INDUSTRIES OPERATING 
DURING THE FIRST SIX MONTHS OF THIS YEAR. 

THE 22-NATION INTERNATIONAL RAW MATERIALS CONFERENCE MADE THE 
ALLOCATION AND IN ADDITION ASSIGNED THE UNITED STATES 47 PER CENT OF 
SCARCE TUNGSTEN SUPPLIES FOR THE SAME PERIOD. | 

IN ANNOUNCING THE ALLOCATIONS; THE CONFERENCE SAID PRODUCTION OF 
BOTH METALS, ESSENTIAL FOR HARDENING STEEL, HAS INCREASED DURING THE 
PAST YEAR AS A RESULT OF STEPPED-UP PRODUCTION AND CONSERVATION 
EFFORTS. MOLYBDENUM SUPPLIES HAVE INCREASED 20 PER CENT DURING THE 
PAST YEAR, IT SAID, AND TUNGSTEN 80 PER CENT COMPARED WITH THE FIRST 
QUARTER OF 1951. °.

WASHINGTON, MARCH 31-(AP)-THE DEFENSE DEPARTMENT TODAY OUTLIN- 
ED FURTHER THE NEW ROTATION POLICY FOR TROOPS_LN.KOREA, RECENTLY ANNOUNG 

BY THE EIGHTH ARMY. 

e THE PENTAGON SAID THE NEW POLICY WAS ADOPTED PARTLY BECAUSE ARMY 
MANPOWER AND BUDGET REQUIREMENTS HAVE LEFT FEWER TROOPS AVAILABLE FOR 
REPLACEMENTS AND REQUIRED REDUCING THE NUMBER OF MEN WHO CAN BE ROTAT- 
ED MONTHLY FROM KOREA, THE ARMY SAID TODAY. 

THE NEW POLICY ALSO IS INTENDED "TO OBTAIN A MORE EQUITABLE SYSTEM 
OF AWARDING SERVICE CREDITS BASED ON HARDSHIPS AND HAZARDS ACTUALLY 
ENCOUNTERED BY INDIVIDUALS IN KOREA,* AN ARMY STATEMENT SAID. | 

UNDER THE NEW POLICY A MAN MUST STILL OBTAIN A MINIMUM OF 36 "CON- 
STRUCTIVE MONTHS SERVICE (CMS)*" TO BE ELIGIBLE FOR ROTATION TO THE 
UNITED STATES. BUT EFFECTIVE APRIL 1 THE CMS CREDITS ARE DIVIDED AMONG 
THREE ZONES INSTEAD OF TWO AS REFORE. | | 

THE NEWLY DESIGNATED ZONE IS THE "INTERMEDIATE COMBAT ZONE,” IN 
WHICH THREE CMS CREDITS ARE AWARDED FOR EACH MONTHS' SERVICE. THIS 
WILL INCLUDE, THE ARMY SAYS, "AREAS IN WHICH TROOPS ARE NOT OFTEN EX- 
POSED TO EXTREME COMBAT HAZARDS, BUT IN WHICH THEY MUST LIVE UNDER 
COMPARATIVELY RIGOROUS CONDITIONS." THE MEN IN THIS AREA ARE "COMBAT 

|-PERSONNEL WHO ARE NOT CONTINUALLY EXPOSED TO DIRECT ENEMY FIRE, INCLUD- 

# ING ALL OTHER DIVISION PERSONNEL OPERATING FORWARD OF DIVISION MAIN 
HEADQUARTERS WITH ATTACHED UNITS, SUCH AS ARTILLERY BATTALIONS, COMBAT 
ENGINEER UNITS, AND SERVICE SUPPORT UNITS." 

THE TWO ZONES ESTABLISHED UNDER THE RULE RULE HAVE BEEN MODIFIED 
SO THAT A
